title: Claude Completes Full 13-Million-Line Lean 4 Formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 11 Days
whyItMatters: Dozens of Claude agents formalized Wiles–Taylor’s complete proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem—13 million lines and 30,300 theorems, 5× Mathlib’s size—in just 11 days.
summary: Anthropic deployed a coordinated fleet of Claude agents that wrote ~13 million lines of Lean 4 code (~6 billion output tokens, ~30,300 proved lemmas) to complete the first full computer-verified proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 11 days—a milestone human formalization leaders like Kevin Buzzard had projected would take years. Buzzard reviewed the top-level theorem and architecture, cementing multi-agent Lean synthesis as the backbone for certifying massive proofs.
technicalHighlights: Generated ~13 million lines of kernel-checked Lean 4 (>5× the entire Mathlib library) in 11 days with minimal human mathematical guidance.
Formally verified Andrew Wiles and Richard Taylor’s modularity-lifting proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem.
Directly proved the multi-million-line Lean infrastructure that enabled rapid certification of the November 2026 Riemann Hypothesis proof.
caveats: Formalizes an established 1995 human theorem rather than discovering new mathematics; the 13M-line codebase is far more verbose than curated human Mathlib code.

scoreRationale.foundational: Achieved the first complete formal verification of one of modern mathematics’ most intricate proofs.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrated industrial-scale Lean formalization capability that immediately unlocked RH and massive proof auditing.
scoreRationale.verification: Compiled and checked by Lean 4 kernel and reviewed by Kevin Buzzard.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed a multi-year global human formalization roadmap into an 11-day autonomous agent run.
